1  Common Prayer:
 Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173 of the Mo  Vehicles Act, 1988, to enhance and set aside the award against the jud  and decree dated 14.09.2021 and made in MACTOP.Nos.4701, 4665, 4697 an  4585 of 2017 respectively on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tri  Special Sub Court-2, Motor Vehicle Claims Petitions, Court of Small Ca  Chennai.
 For Appellant  in all appeals : Mr.A.G.F.Terry Chella Raja  For Respondent  in all appeals : R1  Notice dispensed with  Mr.J.Chandran for R2  COMMON JUDGMENT
These appeals have been filed challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MACTOP.Nos.4701, 4665, 4697 and 4585 of 2017 dated 14.09.2021 2.

The learned counsel for the appellants would submit that on 21.04.2017, while all the claimants were interacting with the Circle Inspector https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.958, 962,
971 & 972 of 2023 with regard to sand smuggling at Tirupati-Srikalahasti Road, Yerpedu, a lorry bearing Registration No.AP-26-TD-8679 came in a rash and negligent manner and ran over some of the people.
Due to the said accident, the appellants in CMA.Nos.958, 962 and 971 of 2023 had sustained amputation and the appellant in CMA.No.972 of 2023 had sustained severe fracture.

Considering all the aspects the Tribunal had awarded the following compensation:
CMA.No.958 of 2023:
S.No Particulars Compensation (Rs.) 1 Disability 14,70,000 2 Pain and Sufferings 50,000 3 Transportation 5,000 4 Medical Expenses 11,998 5 Extra Nourishment 10,000 6 Attender Charges 25,500 Total 15,72,498 Rounded off 15,72,500 CMA.No.962 of 2023:

972 of 2023 3.
In the present case, there is no dispute with regard to the negligence and liability.
The only challenge involved in these appeals is with regard to the quantum of compensation.

Considering the injuries sustained by the claimants, the Tribunal had awarded compensation towards loss of income by applying multiplier method in three appeals viz CMA.Nos.958, 962 and 971 of 2023, whereas in CMA.No.972 of 2023, the Tribunal had awarded the compensation by applying percentage method.

The grievance of the claimants is with regard to the fixation meager amount as notional income while awarding the compensation towards loss of income in CMA.Nos.958, 962 and 971 of 2023.
5.
The learned counsel for the claimant would submit that in all the matters, the Tribunal had taken a sum of Rs.10,000/- as notional income for awarding compensation, which is on lower side.

Hence,
he would request this Court to fix a sum of Rs.15,000/- as notional income of all the claimants.

sentences.text: Further, he would submit that the amount awarded towards the disability in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.958, 962, 971 & 972 of 2023 CMA.No.972 of 2023 also appears to be low and hence, requests this Court to enhance the same.

6. In reply, the learned counsel for the respondent would fairly submit that not more than a sum of Rs.12,000/- may be fixed as notional income in all the appeals if this Court is intend to enhance the notional income.

7. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants and the respondent and also perused the materials available on record.
8.

As far as CMA.No.958 of 2023 is concerned, since the accident was occurred in the year 2017 and the age of the claimant at the time of accident is about 44 years, this Court is inclined to fix a sum of Rs.13,500/- as notional income.

Therefore, by applying multiplier as 14 and adding 25% future prospects and taking 80% as functional disability, the loss of income would be calculated as follows:
Rs.13,500/- (notional income) + Rs.3,375/- (25% future prospects) * 12 (months) *
14 (multiplier) * 80/100 (functional disability) = Rs.22,68,000/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.958, 962, 971 & 972 of 2023 9.

As far as CMA.No.962 of 2023 is concerned, since the accident was occurred in the year 2017 and the age of the claimant at the time of accident is about 53 years, this Court is inclined to fix a sum of Rs.13,500/- as notional income.

Therefore, by applying multiplier as 11 and adding 10% future prospects and taking 80% as functional disability, the loss of income would be calculated as follows:
Rs.13,500/- (notional income) + Rs.1,350/- (25% future prospects) * 12 (months) * 11 (multiplier) * 80/100 (functional disability) = Rs.15,68,150/-
10.

As far as CMA.No.971 of 2023 is concerned, since the accident was occurred in the year 2017 and the age of the claimant at the time of accident is about 55 years, this Court is inclined to fix a sum of Rs.13,500/- as notional income.

Therefore, by applying multiplier as 11 and adding 10% future prospects and taking 80% as functional disability, the loss of income would be calculated as follows:
Rs.13,500/- (notional income) + Rs.1,350/- (25% future prospects) * 12 (months) * 11 (multiplier) * 80/100 (functional disability) = Rs.15,68,150/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.958, 962, 971 & 972 of 2023 11.
With regard to all the other heads in CMA.Nos.958, 962 and 971 of 2023 are concerned, the same appears to be just and fair and hence, the same stands confirmed.

12. As far as CMA.No.972 of 2023 is concerned, since this is a special case, considering the facts and circumstances of this matter, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal had rightly applied Savali Dhamodaram vs T.Ramesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79975750/
4 percentage method and awarded the compensation towards disability by taking 40% as functional disability.

sentences.text: However, this Court feels that the amount awarded by the Tribunal i.e., a sum of Rs.5,000/- per percentage appears to be on the lower side and hence, the same stands enhanced to a sum of Rs.7,000/- per percentage.

Accordingly, the loss of income would be calculated as follows:
Rs.7,000/- (amount per percentage) * 40 (percentage) = Rs.2,80,000/-
13.
Further, it appears that no amount was awarded towards loss of amenities.
Hence, this Court is inclined to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards the same.
With regard to all the other heads, the compensation awarded by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A.Nos.958, 962, 971 & 972 of 2023 Tribunal appears to be just and reasonable.
Hence, the same stands confirmed.
